## Guinness World Records: Lowest Ranked ATP Tour Title Winner
Summarized by Meta AI
52 people talking about this
Marin Cilic holds the record as the lowest ranked ATP Tour title winner after winning the 2024 Hangzhou Open at World No. 777. For Grand Slams, Mark Edmondson remains the lowest ranked winner at No. 212 when he took the 1976 Australian Open.
Marin Cilic's Hangzhou 2024 record at World No. 777
Marin Cilic set the ATP Tour record in September 2024 when he won the Hangzhou Open as a wildcard ranked 777th in the world. The Croatian former world No. 3 defeated Zhang Zhizhen in the final, then jumped 565 places to No. 212 in the rankings. It was his 21st career title and first since 2021.

Mark Edmondson and the Grand Slam record at No. 212
While Cilic holds the ATP Tour record, the lowest ranked Grand Slam singles champion is Mark Edmondson. The Australian won the 1976 Australian Open ranked No. 212, beating defending champion John Newcombe in four sets. He remains the lowest-ranked winner of a Grand Slam tournament since ATP rankings began in 1973.

Other notable low-ranked ATP title winners
Cilic's 777 ranking tops the list, but several other players have won ATP titles from well outside the top 300. The graphic below shows Lleyton Hewitt won Adelaide 1998 at No. 550, Pablo Andujar took Marrakech 2018 at No. 355, Fernando Gonzalez won Orlando 2000 at No. 352, and Tommy Haas captured Houston 2004 at No. 349.

How Cilic's ranking jump compares
Cilic's victory was historic not just for the ranking but for the size of the leap. No player had ever gone up 565 places in the rankings after a single tournament. The win came after a long injury layoff for the 2014 US Open champion, who had been ranked as high as No. 3 in 2018.
